messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Threat
  - Triggers → Memory
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals → Memory
  - Negative Appraisals → Triggers
  - Memory → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Memory → Threat
  - Memory → Negative Appraisals
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Memory
  - Threat → Negative Appraisals
  - Threat → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Memory
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Threat

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Sameer was twenty-two when the mortar round shattered his world. He had been unloading crates in a makeshift market when the earth bucked beneath his boots, and the initial blast ripped the air before a cascade of concussive bangs vibrated through his chest. What frightened him most was the suffocating lack of control as dust choked his lungs and the ground turned to rubble. In that suspended moment, the smell of cordite and burning rubber clung to his clothes, while the sudden violence of the explosion sounds convinced him that nothing in his life felt meaningful anymore and that the world was a dangerous place. Those appraisals did not stay abstract. Every time he caught that phantom scent of smoke on a city street or heard a car backfire, the olfactory and auditory triggers instantly pulled the traumatic memory into sharp relief, dragging him back to the market. His body would lock into the exact crouch he had held while crawling over shattered concrete, and the overwhelming grief of losing his comrades rose in his chest until it felt impossible to draw air. Because the story of that day felt so extreme that it was hard to believe it actually happened to him, he told himself he had fractured beyond repair. As weeks stretched into months, this cycle calcified into a rigid routine. His belief that the world was a dangerous place left him perpetually scanning his environment, which magnified ordinary smells and sudden bangs into severe triggers. His hypervigilance—being superalert and watchful—ensured that his body felt constantly tense and ready to react to danger, which in turn kept his threat system primed for the next trigger. This relentless alertness fed the memories, making him startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people, while the resulting flashbacks immediately deepened his conviction that he was no longer capable of doing the things that defined him. Feeling trapped in a dangerous world with a body that never rested, he adopted a new routine. To outrun the paralyzing sense of lost meaning and the crushing grief on recall, he worked hard at keeping busy with other things, scrubbing surfaces and driving himself through double shifts, while strictly avoiding news reports about events similar to what happened to him. Yet this busyness did not silence the storm. His rumination about why the event happened to him left him mentally looping over the past, which inadvertently heightened his sensitivity to triggers and kept his threat responses active. Each avoided headline and each frantic work session maintained his state of tension, ensuring that when a memory did surface, his body on alert would flare instantly, deepening his conviction that he was no longer capable. The more he tried to stay occupied and avoid the news, the more his maladaptive strategies inadvertently primed his nervous system, causing the traumatic memories to break through with greater intensity. Now fifty-three, Sameer spends his days restoring murals in a historic community center, but the trade has become a minefield. Standing on scaffolding to match pigments, he is hyper-vigilant and watchful, his eyes darting to the street below where delivery doors slam with sudden explosion sounds that make him jump at ordinary noises. He knows he cannot sustain this pace. He finally came to the clinic because his wife found him pacing the driveway at 3 a.m., breathless and convinced he smelled burning rubber, while he sat with her at the kitchen table admitting he was terrified the grief would swallow him whole if he stopped running. What he hopes for is a quiet mind; what he fears is that stepping onto a ladder will be the moment everything collapses again, pulling him back to the exact position he held on that shattered street.
